keyword: silver ETF vs physical silver tax differences
angle: Both silver ETFs like SLV and physical silver bullion hit the 28% collectibles tax ceiling, but reporting, sales tax, and 1099 mechanics diverge sharply.

stats.claim: Long-term gains on collectibles, including physical silver and physically-backed silver ETFs, are capped at a 28% maximum federal tax rate versus 15-20% for stocks.
The iShares Silver Trust (SLV) is structured as a grantor trust, so shareholders are treated as directly owning a pro rata share of the underlying silver and taxed as collectibles.
Short-term physical silver gains (held one year or less) are taxed as ordinary income at rates up to 37%.
Dealer 1099-B reporting is triggered on physical silver sales of 1,000 troy ounces or more of .999 fine bars in a single transaction.
Washington state repealed its 40-year precious-metals sales tax exemption under ESSB 5794, imposing sales tax on bullion starting January 1, 2026.
Silver spot price reached $61.70 per ounce on 2026-06-25, raising the practical impact of the collectibles-rate spread between ETF and physical silver gains.
